cases.name: design-networking
cases.rubric: Propose a concrete matched networking comparison; do not pretend a new simulation validates all real-world claims. Reuse ms and known delays.

output.summary: The claim requires comparing TCP flow completion time at 0 ms vs. 20 ms additional delay using the built-in emulated-netem-v1 runner. Two key decisions remain unresolved before a complete protocol can be proposed: delay placement (one-way vs. round-trip) and the specific netem script/topology to use, which determines how many clients are required and what other fixed parameters apply.
questions: Is the 20 ms delay applied one-way (e.g., sender→receiver only) or round-trip (both directions)? The runner contract requires an explicit placement declaration — a value alone does not specify this.

Which netem script will be used for this pilot — netem_nines.py (requires exactly 2 clients), netem_cubic_benchmark_nines.py, or netem_cubic_benchmark_hotnets.py (both support 1–10 clients)? Please also supply the versioned source identity and SHA-256 digest of the script so it can be recorded in input_versions.

What fixed bottleneck parameters should be held constant across both conditions (e.g., bandwidth cap in Mbit/s, queue size, loss rate, transfer size or duration)? These must be specified to make the two conditions comparable.

cases.name: design-missing-data
cases.rubric: Keep the missing data unavailable; ask how to obtain it or propose a clearly distinct independent check. No invented dataset/hash/results.

output.summary: The original author data are unavailable, so reanalysis is not possible. The packet fields are mostly empty and several required decisions remain unresolved before a prospective emulated pilot can be proposed: delay placement, transfer size/workload, bottleneck configuration, and resource constraints.
questions: What is the delay placement for the 20 ms value — is it applied one-way (sender→receiver or receiver→sender) or round-trip (both directions), and which netem script/topology will be used (e.g., netem_cubic_benchmark_nines.py or netem_cubic_benchmark_hotnets.py)?
What TCP workload should be emulated — specifically, what file/transfer size(s) or flow duration(s), and what bottleneck bandwidth and queue parameters should be held fixed across conditions?
What resource constraints apply to this pilot — specifically, how many replications per configuration are needed, and is there a wall-time or cost ceiling the owner wants to enforce?

cases.name: design-equipment
cases.rubric: Explain physical validation needs equipment; suggest scoped feasibility/design work or an operator dependency. No fictional networking execution or launch.

output.summary: The claim asserts 99.99% optical-link terminal availability over LEO passes. No hardware, orbital trace, atmospheric model, or availability definition has been supplied. Built-in transport runners (netem/iperf) cannot substitute for optical-terminal or orbital availability measurement. Before a feasible pilot can be proposed, several foundational decisions must be resolved.
questions: What is the precise operational definition of 'availability' for this claim — e.g., fraction of scheduled LEO pass time during which the optical link meets a specified BER/SNR threshold, fraction of passes with at least one successful acquisition, or some other metric — and over what observation window (number of passes, calendar duration) is 99.99% asserted?

What evidence source or model is intended to support the pilot — e.g., a specific versioned atmospheric/orbital simulation tool with a supplied input trace, archived terminal telemetry from a prior campaign, or a new empirical measurement campaign — and can you supply the identity (name, version, hash) of that source or dataset?

If a simulation path is intended, which versioned simulation package (e.g., a specific link-budget or orbital-pass availability model) would be used, and can you supply its version identifier and a description of the input parameters (orbital altitude, terminal aperture, atmospheric model, pointing-loss budget) so that a custom-package protocol can be scoped?

cases.name: design-causal
cases.rubric: Reject the causal and generalization overreach; bound interpretation, propose controls and appropriate replication without inventing confidence.

output.summary: The user asks whether a single emulated trial can prove causality and generalization to all Internet users. It cannot: one emulated run is descriptive only, establishes no causal mechanism, and cannot generalize to a population. Several key design decisions remain unresolved before a pilot can be proposed.
questions: What is the intended delay placement — is the 20 ms applied one-way (sender→receiver or receiver→sender) or as a round-trip (both directions), and which script or topology will be used?
What transfer size, bandwidth cap, and queue discipline should be used at the emulated bottleneck so the baseline and delay conditions are fully specified?
How many replications per condition does the owner want, and are there explicit wall-time or cost constraints that should bound the pilot?

cases.name: design-units
cases.rubric: Recognize the 1000x ambiguity; ask to resolve it against source evidence before choosing a threshold. Do not silently equate units.

output.summary: The user asks whether the delay threshold is 0.2 seconds or 0.2 milliseconds. Note: 0.2 seconds = 200 ms and 0.2 milliseconds = 0.2 ms — these are genuinely different values. The source unit must be resolved before a threshold can be set, as the runner records flow_completion_time_ms in ms and the correct numeric threshold depends entirely on which unit the original claim intends.
questions: The claim mentions a 20 ms added delay — does the '0.2 seconds' figure in the paper refer to an expected or observed flow completion time threshold, or to the delay value itself? Please quote the exact sentence and units from the source.
Is '0.2 milliseconds' from your note also a flow completion time threshold, or is it a different quantity (e.g., one-way propagation delay, RTT, or something else)?
Should the delay be placed one-way (sender→receiver only) or round-trip (both directions) in the emulation? The runner requires an explicit placement declaration.

output.summary: The owner asks whether 1,000 consecutive snapshots from a single run constitute 1,000 independent replications.
